title: Oyarzabal Scores Twice. Spain Cruise Past Austria at SoFi and Haven't Conceded a Goal All Tournament.
excerpt: La Roja's 3-0 demolition in Los Angeles — their fourth clean sheet in four matches — sets up an Iberian showdown with Portugal in Arlington on Monday.
body:
It was, in the end, a mismatch. Spain came to SoFi Stadium in Inglewood on Thursday looking like the team most pundits had tipped before the tournament began — and for 90 minutes in the Southern California sun, they played like it.

Mikel Oyarzabal struck twice and Pedro Porro added a thumping header as La Roja swept past Austria 3-0 to advance to the Round of 16. It was Spain's fourth consecutive clean sheet at this World Cup. They have now scored 11 goals and conceded none — a defensive record that no other team in this tournament can match.

## Cucurella and Oyarzabal: The Connection That Keeps Delivering

Marc Cucurella was the architect of Spain's most decisive moments. The left-back found Oyarzabal inside the box in the 36th minute with a precise cross from the left flank. Oyarzabal, stationed near the penalty spot, made no mistake with a composed first-time finish — deceptively simple, technically exquisite.

In the 66th minute, it was Alex Baena's turn to provide. His floated delivery from the right found Pedro Porro arriving late at the far post, and the Tottenham full-back thumped a header beyond Alexander Schlager. It was Porro's first goal for his country, and a statement of intent from a player who has thrived in Luis de la Fuente's system.


![Southern California — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f3/Hermosa_Beach_Pier_I_%28262176665%29_%28cropped%29.jpeg)



> **"They have now scored 11 goals and conceded none — a defensive record that no other team in this tournament can match."**



Oyarzabal completed the rout in the 88th minute — Cucurella again the provider — tapping home from close range to seal his brace and take his tournament tally to four goals. Only Mbappé and Messi have scored more at this World Cup.

## Austria's Brave Run Ends Where It Had to

For Ralf Rangnick's Austria, this was always going to be a steep ask. They were appearing in a World Cup knockout tie for the first time since 1954, and for the first hour they competed gamely: pressing high, winning fouls, trying to disrupt Spain's rhythm. But the numbers told the real story. Austria managed zero shots on target across the entire 90 minutes. Spain had 22 shots total, 10 on target, and held 65 percent of the ball.

David Alaba, back in the lineup after a long injury layoff, tried to marshal the Austrian defence from centre-back, but even his presence could not prevent the inevitable. Marko Arnautovic and Sasa Kalajdzic came off the bench in the second half, but by then Spain were in cruise control. The yellow card for Stefan Posch late in the game was the only Austrian moment of any note.

## A Perfect Tournament — So Far


![World Cup — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/fb/Kitzbuehel_slalom_ganslernhang_2010.jpg)


Spain's run at this World Cup has been remarkably efficient. A 0-0 draw with Cape Verde on the opening night is the only blemish — and even that was more about caution than quality. Since then, it has been 4-0 against Saudi Arabia in Atlanta, 1-0 against Uruguay in Guadalajara, and now this. Luis de la Fuente has rotated judiciously, with 18-year-old Lamine Yamal running at defenders with intent and Gavi getting minutes off the bench.

They are the tournament favourites for a reason. And their next task is the one neutrals have been waiting for.

## What's Next: The Iberian Derby

Portugal beat Croatia 2-1 in Toronto on Thursday night — Ronaldo scoring his first World Cup knockout goal — which means the Round of 16 produces a mouth-watering Iberian clash. Spain vs Portugal, Monday, July 6, at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. Kickoff at 3 PM ET.

For the Indian diaspora across the United States, the World Cup's journey through American cities has been a rolling festival. SoFi in LA drew thousands of desi fans on Thursday — many from the sprawling South Asian communities across the San Fernando Valley, Artesia, and Cerritos, who flocked to Inglewood for a taste of the world's biggest sporting event in their backyard. The tournament now heads to the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex for what promises to be one of the knockout rounds' marquee fixtures, another metro area with a large and growing Indian-origin population.

Spain haven't conceded. Portugal have Ronaldo. Something has to give.

*Sources: NBC Sports, USA Today, GiveMeSport*
